Built for a manual closed loop

Flux = slope × P × V / (R × T × A). CO₂ slopes use ppm/s and return µmol m⁻² s⁻¹; CH₄ slopes use ppb/s and return nmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Pressure is converted from kPa to Pa, temperature from °C to K, and volume from litres to m³. Positive flux indicates emission; negative indicates uptake.

Use chamber air temperature and absolute chamber/ambient pressure. CAVITY_T and CAVITY_P describe the analyser and are never auto-filled here. Imported concentrations are used as reported; no extra water-vapour correction is applied.
Effective volume = chamber headspace + collar headspace above the soil + tubing / loop dead volume. Do not include the buried collar volume. Soil area is the collar’s internal cross-sectional area.

Select closure start and end times, then exclude an initial mixing period. Review the trace and R² for leaks, curvature and unstable fits. This version uses ordinary linear regression; it does not automatically detect closures or fit nonlinear chamber models. Data stays in this browser; export a backup. Map tiles require internet access.
